purpose: Flatten religious lineage nodes into a chronology suitable for timeline and spiral rendering while preserving uncertainty, parentage and node type.

projection_rules.one_node_one_seed_clock: Each lineage node contributes one primary seed/formation clock here; additional councils, migrations, institutional reorganizations and refoundations belong in later event expansions.
projection_rules.uncertain_dates: Ranges remain ranges and should render as bands/arcs, not exact points.
projection_rules.branch_relation: parent_ids + relation_to_parent determine where a child trajectory attaches to an ancestral trajectory.
projection_rules.no_rank: Chronological radius encodes time only; it does not encode spiritual worth, truth, importance or authority.
projection_rules.historical_year_zero: Display logic must skip year zero when converting negative sort integers into BCE/CE labels.

events.name: Vedic religious field
events.notes: Deep substrate; not identical to later Hinduism.

events.name: Zoroastrian tradition / Zarathustra-associated reform
events.date_or_range: plausible scholarly range c. 13th–6th century BCE; many favor around 1000 BCE
events.place: eastern Iranian / Central Asian region, uncertain
events.notes: Must render as a wide uncertainty band; exact date and place remain debated.

events.name: Israelite/Judahite religious formation
events.notes: Deep substrate rather than a single founded religion.

events.name: Jain / Jina tradition, Mahavira-associated historical formation
events.notes: Jain tradition remembers earlier Tirthankaras; historical reconstruction should preserve that sacred chronology separately.

events.name: Post-exilic / Persian-period Judaism
events.notes: Torah/scriptural authority and portable communal forms become increasingly central.

events.name: Second Temple Jewish field
events.date_or_range: Second Temple period, c. 516 BCE–70 CE
events.notes: A plural religious field, not one denomination.

events.name: Early Buddhist sangha
events.notes: Historical Buddha chronology is debated; avoid one exact birthday.

events.name: Samaritan Israelite tradition
events.notes: Do not render Samaritanism as a denomination born from rabbinic Judaism.

events.name: Hindu traditions / long formation
events.date_or_range: late Vedic, epic, Puranic and devotional formation, broad window
events.notes: No single founder or seed date; 'Hinduism' is a later umbrella for many interacting traditions.

events.name: Classical Daoist textual field
events.notes: Daodejing/Zhuangzi textual-philosophical formation predates organized Daoist religious institutions; 'philosophical vs religious Daoism' is a modern simplification but chronology still matters.

events.name: Vaishnava traditions
events.date_or_range: late centuries BCE–early centuries CE crystallization
events.notes: Includes multiple Vishnu/Krishna/Rama devotional and theological lineages.

events.name: Sri Lankan Theravada-associated monastic lineage
events.date_or_range: 3rd century BCE transmission to Sri Lanka
events.notes: Theravada as a modern umbrella should not be projected unchanged onto all ancient communities.

events.name: Shaiva traditions
events.date_or_range: late centuries BCE–early centuries CE crystallization
events.notes: Vedic Rudra background and multiple later Shaiva sectarian/philosophical systems.

events.name: Mahayana movements
events.date_or_range: c. 1st century BCE–2nd century CE emergence
events.notes: Early Mahayana likely involved loose currents within existing monasteries, not an immediate separate church.

events.name: Śvetāmbara Jain tradition
events.date_or_range: early centuries CE → late-5th-century textual stabilization
events.notes: The split with Digambara is not securely reducible to one exact year.

events.name: Digambara Jain tradition
events.notes: Later sectarian narratives of one dramatic split are historically difficult; use gradual differentiation.

events.name: Early Christianity / Jesus movement
events.notes: Historically emerges within the Second Temple Jewish world and rapidly becomes translocal.

events.name: Rabbinic Judaism
events.notes: Do not model Pharisees as a proven one-step parent. Mishnah c. 200; rabbinization is gradual and much later.

events.name: East Asian Buddhist transmission field
events.date_or_range: early centuries CE transmission into China → major Chinese schools from c. 6th century onward
events.place: Central Asia / China / Korea / Japan / Vietnam
events.notes: Context node for networked transmission; should not replace specific school histories.

events.name: Way of the Celestial Masters
events.date_or_range: 142 CE traditional foundation marker → late-Han community formation
events.notes: First Daoist religious organization for which substantial documentation survives; 142 is a traditional/organizational marker rather than origin of all Daoist religion.

events.name: Shakta traditions
events.date_or_range: c. 4th–7th centuries CE major textual/sectarian crystallization
events.notes: Goddess worship is older than this window; this marks stronger sectarian/textual crystallization, not first goddess devotion.

events.name: Nicene Christian consolidation
events.place: Nicaea / Constantinople and Roman imperial church networks
events.notes: Council markers are doctrinal consolidation events, not the birth of all churches receiving them.

events.name: Shangqing / Highest Clarity tradition
events.notes: Textual/revelatory corpus emphasizing visualization and inner deities; incorporates earlier traditions rather than descending simply from Celestial Masters.

events.name: Lingbao / Numinous Treasure tradition
events.notes: Strong communal ritual and salvation orientation; integrates Celestial Master, Shangqing and Buddhist elements.

events.name: Pure Land traditions
events.date_or_range: Mahayana Pure Land practices/text networks develop in China; distinct Japanese schools crystallize especially 12th–13th centuries
events.notes: Pure Land is a trans-Asian family of practices and texts, not one coherent denomination; Japanese Jōdo/Jōdo Shin institutions are later specific formations.

events.name: Church of the East lineage
events.notes: Ancient Mesopotamian Christianity predates 431; the council is a differentiation marker, not an origin from nothing.

events.name: Chalcedonian Christian family
events.notes: Receives the Chalcedonian definition.

events.name: Oriental Orthodox / non-Chalcedonian communion family
events.place: Egypt, Syria, Armenia and connected regions
events.notes: Constituent churches have pre-451 roots; 451 marks enduring non-reception of Chalcedon, not their creation ex nihilo.

events.name: Vajrayana / tantric Buddhist traditions
events.place: South Asia → Tibet/Himalaya and wider Asia
events.notes: Multiple tantric textual and practice lineages; no single founder.

events.name: Latin Western Christian tradition
events.notes: Gradual linguistic, political, canonical and ecclesiological differentiation.

events.name: Greek/Eastern Chalcedonian tradition
events.notes: Gradual differentiation; includes multiple patriarchates/churches, not one ethnicity.

events.name: Chan / Zen traditions
events.date_or_range: 7th–8th centuries CE institutional formation in China
events.place: China → Korea, Japan, Vietnam and wider transmission
events.notes: Chan institutional identity crystallizes in China through the 7th–8th centuries; later Zen, Seon and Thiền are regionally distinct transmission histories, not one unchanged school.

events.name: Tibetan Buddhist traditions
events.date_or_range: first transmission from 7th century; later transmission from 10th–12th centuries
events.notes: Tibetan Buddhism receives Indian Mahayana and Vajrayana transmissions over centuries; Nyingma and later Sakya/Kagyu/Gelug/Jonang histories should be carved separately.

events.name: Early Islam / Qur'anic community
events.notes: 622 Hijra is a particularly strong community/institutional clock inside this formation.

events.name: Shiʿi / Alid-imamate traditions
events.date_or_range: 632 succession dispute; 680 Karbala as major formative marker
events.place: Medina / Kufa / Karbala and wider networks
events.notes: Shiʿi identity and doctrine develop through several succession crises and imamate lineages.

events.name: Sunni Islam, formative majority tradition
events.place: Medina, Damascus, Baghdad and wider caliphal networks
events.notes: Do not represent Sunni Islam as fully formed on the day of Muhammad's death; later hadith, law and theology crystallize over centuries.

events.name: Kharijite / Muhakkima early current
events.notes: Early third trajectory distinct from both later Sunni and Shiʿi authority structures.

events.name: Ibadi Islam
events.notes: Historical scholarship relates Ibadism to early Muhakkima/Kharijite fields; Ibadis developed distinct self-understanding and jurisprudence, so avoid using 'Kharijite' as a simplistic present-day label.

events.name: Sufi / tasawwuf currents
events.notes: Cross-cuts Sunni and Shiʿi histories; later tariqas/orders should be modeled as descendant institutional lineages, not as a third Sunni/Shia denomination.

events.name: Zaydi Shiʿism
events.date_or_range: 740 CE revolt of Zayd and subsequent lineage formation
events.notes: Use 740 as a major marker, not a claim that all Zaydi doctrine/institutions appeared instantly.

events.name: Karaite Judaism
events.notes: Scripture-centered non-rabbinic Jewish movement; Anan ben David is important but sole-founder narratives should remain qualified.

events.name: Hanafi legal school
events.place: Kufa / Baghdad and wider eastern networks
events.notes: Named for Abu Hanifa (d. 767); school formation continues through students and later jurists.

events.name: Maliki legal school
events.notes: Named for Malik b. Anas (d. 795); regional institutionalization continues later.

events.name: Ismaili Shiʿism
events.date_or_range: post-765 succession differentiation; organized daʿwa by 9th century
events.notes: Linked to succession after Jaʿfar al-Sadiq (d. 765); later Fatimid and missionary institutions transform the movement.

events.name: Shafiʿi legal school
events.notes: Named for al-Shafiʿi (d. 820); later jurists consolidate the school.

events.name: Hanbali legal school
events.notes: Named for Ahmad ibn Hanbal (d. 855); later jurists institutionalize the madhhab.

events.name: Twelver / Imami Shiʿism
events.place: Samarra / Baghdad and wider Imami networks
events.notes: Occultation crisis strongly shapes Twelver theological/institutional crystallization; earlier Imami lineage predates 874.

events.name: Zhengyi / Orthodox Unity
events.date_or_range: medieval umbrella consolidation; Longhushan authority especially Song–Yuan
events.place: Longhushan and southern Chinese ritual networks
events.notes: Later umbrella for multiple register/ritual lineages rooted in Celestial Master traditions; alongside Quanzhen, one of the principal living Daoist formations.

events.name: Roman Catholic Church, post-schism Western trajectory
events.notes: Do not present 1054 as the date the Roman Church itself first existed.

events.name: Eastern Orthodox communion, post-schism trajectory
events.notes: 1054 is a conventional marker in a centuries-long separation; 1204 further hardened it.

events.name: Nizari Ismaili lineage
events.notes: Emerges from the 1094 Nizar/Mustaʿli succession split.

events.name: Mustaʿli Ismaili lineage
events.place: Cairo → Yemen / western India in later developments
events.notes: Later Tayyibi and other developments require their own children.

events.name: Medieval Kabbalistic currents
events.place: southern France / Iberia and wider Jewish networks
events.notes: Cross-cutting mystical traditions, not a denomination.

events.name: Quanzhen / Complete Perfection
events.date_or_range: 1160s CE founding phase under Wang Chongyang
events.notes: Monastic/cultivation movement founded by Wang Chongyang and early disciples; develops its own institutions while drawing on wider Daoist, Buddhist and Confucian currents.

events.name: Sikh tradition
events.notes: Community and institutions develop through successive Gurus.

events.name: Protestant Reformation family
events.place: Wittenberg and multiple European reform centers
events.notes: Not one denomination; multiple Reformation streams emerged independently/interactively.

events.name: Lutheran tradition
events.notes: 1530 is a strong confessional consolidation marker.

events.name: Reformed tradition
events.notes: Zwinglian and Calvinian trajectories should not be flattened into one founder/date.

events.name: Anabaptist traditions
events.date_or_range: 21 Jan 1525 Zürich baptisms; 1527 Schleitheim consolidation marker
events.notes: Multiple Radical Reformation streams; Zürich Brethren are a high-information institutional seed.

events.name: Church of England / Anglican trajectory
events.notes: Has both institutional continuity with medieval English Christianity and Reformation-era doctrinal/liturgical transformation.

events.name: English Separatist / Independent field
events.notes: Context node for English congregational/separatist currents; not a denomination.

events.name: Presbyterian traditions
events.notes: A Reformed family especially associated with presbyterial governance; not all Reformed churches are Presbyterian.

events.name: English dissenting / Seeker field
events.notes: Context node for radical Protestant, Seeker and dissenting currents; not one church.

events.name: Baptist traditions
events.notes: Modern Baptist histories commonly use the 1609 Amsterdam congregation as a seed marker; General and Particular Baptist streams develop separately. Do not derive Baptists directly from continental Anabaptists as a simple one-line genealogy.

events.name: Religious Society of Friends / Quaker traditions
events.notes: Friends emerge in the 17th-century English dissenting/Seeker field with strong emphasis on immediate divine guidance, equality and distinctive worship. Later branches differ substantially.

events.name: Khalsa
events.notes: A major refoundation/disciplinary community marker within Sikh history.

events.name: Methodist traditions
events.notes: Begins as an Anglican revival movement; later Methodist denominations institutionalize separately.

events.name: Evangelical movement/current
events.notes: Cross-denominational movement rather than a single church; later evangelical identities diversify substantially.

events.name: Hasidic Judaism
events.place: Podolia and eastern European Jewish communities
events.notes: Baal Shem Tov-associated revival; later diversified into dynastic/group lineages.

events.name: Stone-Campbell / Restoration Movement
events.notes: A restorationist/primitivist movement seeking New Testament church patterns; later trajectories include Disciples of Christ, Churches of Christ and Christian Churches/Churches of Christ.

events.name: Reform / Liberal Judaism
events.notes: Modern movement has earlier precursors; Hamburg gives a strong institutional seed marker, not the sole intellectual origin.

events.name: Orthodox Judaism as modern denominational identity
events.notes: Traditional halakhic practice is far older; 'Orthodox' becomes a modern denominational identity partly through response to Reform/modernity.

events.name: Adventist traditions
events.notes: Adventism is broader than Seventh-day Adventism; 1863 is the SDA organizational date.

events.name: Wesleyan-Holiness movement
events.notes: Transdenominational holiness current emphasizing sanctification/perfect love in Wesleyan trajectories; later feeds Nazarene and some Pentecostal histories.

events.name: Bábí movement
events.notes: Immediate predecessor field of the Baháʼí Faith.

events.name: Baháʼí Faith
events.notes: Baháʼí identity increasingly replaces Bábí after the 1863 declaration.

events.name: Conservative / Masorti Judaism
events.notes: JTS was founded in 1886 and became a central institutional engine; intellectual precursors include nineteenth-century Positive-Historical Judaism.

events.name: Pentecostal movement
events.notes: Heavily shaped by Holiness currents; later becomes globally diverse and cross-denominational.

events.name: Church of the Nazarene
events.notes: A Wesleyan-Holiness denomination formed through union of several holiness bodies; 1908 is the official anniversary marker.

merge_model.lineage_events: Primary lineage-node seed/formation clocks remain in events.
merge_model.notable_events: Load data/religious-foundation-events.json as a second chronological stream.
merge_model.branch_rule: If a notable event creates_or_crystallizes_child_ids, render the child trajectory from that marker while keeping the child's full formation window available.
merge_model.priority: major by default; secondary optional; context hidden unless requested
